target_customer: Independent grocery store owners in the US
problem: Small grocery stores lose money to theft, safety incidents and out-of-stocks and cannot afford staff to watch the store or run ordering and pricing.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus on-premise GPU hardware for camera monitoring

founders.name: Nicholas Sleeper
founders.background_notes: Spent summers in his family's grocery store, which has operated for over 100 years.

founders.name: Prateek Pinisetti
founders.background_notes: Chess National Master, real-time systems expert. Met Sleeper as Harvard roommates per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: On-premise GPU video analytics for theft and safety is standard computer vision engineering, but making it reliable on messy store camera feeds with a two person team is the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: The wedge of camera-based loss prevention was already served by specialist vendors and the broader store manager vision depended on future POS integrations that had not shipped. Family grocery access gave distribution but not a structural moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Loss prevention vendors already sold AI camera analytics to retailers. What happened to Kirana itself is not public.

market_need_then: Retail theft and shrink were a widely covered concern in 2024 and 2025 and independent grocers run thin margins. The founders cite their own family's store as the source of the pain.

branding.domain_note: Used kirana-ai.com, not the exact kirana.com (website field).

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community coverage of the brand found. Search results were dominated by the unrelated Indian company KiranaPro and other Kirana named firms, so the name was confusable.

outcome_analysis: Kirana AI joined YC in Spring 2025 with a two person team and a pitch that mixed camera loss prevention with a longer term AI store manager. The YC directory lists it as acquired, but no acquirer, date or press coverage could be found, and one YC listing still shows it as active. The cause and terms are not public, so no failure factors are recorded.
notes: Status conflict: the YC page fetched says Acquired but a YC search snippet said Active. No acquirer found in two searches, so exit date and acquirer are null. Funding of about 500K pre-seed appears only in VCBacked, one aggregator, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Company website returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Competitor sources found (Veesion, Spot AI comparison pages) are undated vendor pages, so the competitor list is left empty.
